clue.text: Go down and see, as befits one who is wise

definitions.text: as befits one who is wise

parts.note: to go down or droop is to sag
a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is the crossword's favourite one

explanation.surface: An instruction to sink low and look around, in the manner of a wise person.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the stock crossword see (bishop's seat).
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes acting with wisdom, exactly what someone wise would befittingly do.

clue.text: Left wood with lead outside in bag to make bathroom fitting

indicators.note: the whole assembly is placed inside the word for bag

parts.note: a sack is a bag

indicators.note: the lead symbol is split to sit around the left-plus-wood letters

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Timber and lead are bagged up to build a fixture for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps P...B around LASH to give PLASHB, which 'in' sets inside SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashback is the panel behind a basin or bath that protects the wall from water.

clue.text: Squash, say, not right with a particular cheese

indicators.note: not signals that the right letter is left out of the word for squash

parts.note: a squash is an example of a gourd

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish goes wrong when paired with a certain cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from GOURD, leaving GOUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a named Dutch cheese, so a specific variety rather than cheese in general.

clue.text: Famous wartime pilot became so drunk

definitions.meaning: the RAF ace Douglas Bader lost both his legs in a crash

explanation.surface: A celebrated airman ended up thoroughly intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Bader, a British fighter pilot of the Second World War, flew with artificial legs.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is literally without legs, like Bader; the other is the slang for too drunk to stand.

clue.text: Engineers needing time with advantage not initially getting extra component

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for advantage is dropped

parts.note: an advantage or gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Army engineers, pressed for time and seeking gain, are fitted with an additional part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes the P from PROFIT, leaving ROFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrofit is a part added to existing equipment after manufacture, an additional component.

clue.text: Jane keeps island home for birds

indicators.note: the surname holds the island letter within it

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine

explanation.surface: Jane looks after an island bird sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Sports official still falling short as provider of clarification

parts.note: a ref is a referee

indicators.note: the word for still loses its final letter

parts.note: still or motionless means inert

explanation.surface: A referee, still not up to scratch, is asked to clear things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' drops the T from INERT, leaving INER.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner purifies substances such as sugar or oil, clarifying them by removing impurities.

clue.text: Stopping coastal occupation around the province

indicators.note: the trade word goes around the province letters

parts.note: fishing is a typical seaside trade
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province in Britain

explanation.surface: Seaside jobs are ending all over Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing means bringing to an end, the same as stopping.

clue.text: Instruct archer taking very careful aim

definitions.meaning: to instruct someone is to order or direct them
William ..., the Swiss folk hero, shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: Giving orders to a bowman lining up a precise shot.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for ordering someone; the other is the legendary Swiss crossbowman.

clue.text: President once holding key, rising to make a case

indicators.note: the president's name holds the reversed letters within it

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a former US president

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for key is read upwards, last letter first

parts.note: key means crucial or vital

explanation.surface: A former president with a key item stands up to argue his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a legal argument; here it is a grammatical case. 'rising' reads the key word upwards, as fits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is a noun case, expressing means, instrument or separation.

clue.text: See a Parisian dress being worn by bishop in watering-hole

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a Parisian would say un for a

indicators.note: the clothing word is wrapped around the bishop, as though he had it on

parts.note: dress or clothing is gear
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A French-flavoured scene of a bishop dressed up and spotted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being worn by' has the bishop wrapped in the clothing word, as if he had it on.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering-hole is informal for a pub or bar, and a lounge bar is the comfier room of a British pub.

clue.text: Decisive female favoured by small boy

parts.note: to be in is to be in favour or fashionable
Al is a short form of the boy's name Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A decisive woman is preferred by a little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A final result or game is the one that settles matters conclusively, hence decisive.

clue.text: Unruly fan — seems he's cad creating embarrassment

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of these words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy supporter thinks some rotter is causing him awkwardness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shamefaced is looking ashamed, so the noun names a state of embarrassment or sheepishness.

clue.text: See sudden rant turning nasty

indicators.note: these letters turn ugly and are thrown into a different order

explanation.surface: Watch an abrupt tirade become unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or comprehend it, a common synonym.

clue.text: County dandies

definitions.meaning: The short name for Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London
a buck is an old word for a fashionable young man, a dandy

explanation.surface: Fashionable gents from the shires.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the abbreviated English county name, and the plural of an old term for fops.

clue.text: Repetition of tea dance

indicators.note: the tea word is repeated, three copies in a row

parts.note: cha or char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: The same old tea dance, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repetition of' asks for the tea word three times over; the parser can only show one doubling, so the third copy appears as bare letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Sally during trip dumping old sweetheart

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: the former lover is thrown out of the word for trip, as in a break-up

parts.note: a trip or outing is an excursion
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Sally goes off on an outing and ditches her former boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is the definition, a military sortie. 'dumping' removes EX from EXCURSION, leaving CURSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden sortie or raid into enemy territory, a synonym of an incursion.

clue.text: Firm has number given to worker, one sharing room with others?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ten is a number
an ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A company adds staff, and one worker must share an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-tenant shares a rented property with other occupants, so the question mark covers a room.

clue.text: Affected by bingeing and about to have rebuke, you finally fast

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a rap is a sharp rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word you is taken

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: After overindulging, you face a telling-off and must go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent describes suffering from overindulgence in drink or food, hung over and sickly.

clue.text: University has afterthought about performance improvements

indicators.note: the postscript letters wrap around the word for performance

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is an afterthought in a letter
a turn is a performance or act in a show

explanation.surface: A university reconsiders a show that has got better.
explanation.definitionFit: Upturns are rises or recoveries in fortune, i.e. improvements.

clue.text: Truck that is stuck on marshy terrain

indicators.note: the abbreviation is attached to the end of the word for marshy ground

parts.note: a bog is wet marshy ground
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A lorry gets bogged down in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogie is a wheeled undercarriage or low truck, as on railway rolling stock.

clue.text: European region where half of milk goes in black tea

indicators.note: the milk portion is put inside the tea word

parts.note: bohea is an old name for a black China tea

indicators.note: the first two of the four letters of milk are taken

explanation.surface: A place where they add a dash of milk to their black tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohea is a dated name for a black China tea that crosswords still use.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historical region forming the western part of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Chemical process stops this honey becoming runny

indicators.note: runny honey is fluid and loose, so these letters flow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chemical reaction prevents this honey from turning liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants use light to build sugars from carbon dioxide and water, a biochemical process.

clue.text: Setting up of university complex requiring destruction of quiet wood

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means the letters are raised and read bottom to top
the quiet letter is knocked out of the campus word

parts.note: a campus is the grounds and buildings of a university
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Building a campus means felling a peaceful woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring destruction of' removes P from CAMPUS to give CAMUS, which 'Setting up of' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree, and its timber is used in woodwork and tanning.

clue.text: Performer getting cut, a superficial mark

indicators.note: the performer word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: a singer is a performer

explanation.surface: An entertainer suffers a cut, only a minor scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight surface burn, a superficial scorch mark.

clue.text: Blemish reported in engineer's design

indicators.note: reported means as heard spoken, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: a speck is a small spot or blemish

explanation.surface: A flaw was noticed in the engineer's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is the detailed technical description an engineer works to.

clue.text: Power with which star runs — probably a runner to fade?

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
an ace is a star performer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A star athlete's strength looks set to wane.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hints that a pacemaker sets the speed and then usually drops out, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker in a race leads early to set the speed, then typically drops back once the job is done.

clue.text: Record set by fellow, one with a very high level of self-regard

parts.note: a mono is a record in monaural sound
a fellow is a man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A disc made by a chap who thinks very highly of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful reading: a mania for 'mono', one's single self.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an obsession with a single thing, here read whimsically as a craze for the one person, oneself.

clue.text: Female in charge in Civil Service works in traditional library?

indicators.note: the girl and the in-charge letters are placed within the Civil Service abbreviation

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A woman running a government office is at home among the great books.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics are acknowledged great works of literature, the staple of any traditional library.

clue.text: Very last bit of information — there's enthusiasm to collect it

indicators.note: the craze word gathers up the information word inside itself

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze or enthusiasm
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: The final snippet of news, which someone is keen to gather up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is British slang for a cigarette stub, and by extension the leftover tail or remnant of anything.
